content: If you experience vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, or any unexplained bleeding or bruising, you must take immediate action. Regularly check in with public health officials and follow their specific instructions. If you plan to travel more than 50 miles or to another country, inform public health officials in advance. Do not travel on commercial planes, ships, or trains under any circumstances. If you develop a fever of 100.4 degrees Fahrenheit (38 degrees Celsius) or higher, or if you feel like you have a fever or experience other symptoms, contact public health officials immediately. If you are unable to reach a public health official, call a doctor. Inform the doctor about your recent travel history and the possibility of exposure to Ebola. Do not use public transportation to reach a medical facility. Travel only by private car or ambulance. When you arrive at the medical facility, bring this notice with you and provide it to the healthcare staff. (Note: This text is based on CDC recommendations and should be adapted as necessary to align with the protocols of the country in use.)
